label: Domicile type name
summary: Text naming the kind of domicile the character has: 'Manor' or 'Estate'.
details: The entries are game_concept_manor and game_concept_estate. Which one is chosen depends on conditions in the definition, which the game's documentation does not list.

label: Domicile type link
summary: Text naming the character's domicile type as a clickable game-concept link: manor or estate.
details: The entries JAPANESE_MANOR and ESTATE give the texts [manor|E] and [estate|E]; the |E form makes the word a game-concept link. GetDomicileType gives the same two words as plain text.

label: Dominate title wording
summary: Text for a 'dominate' title wording: either 'Dominate' plus the base name of the realm above the character's primary title, or just 'Dominate Title'.
details: The first entry reads the de jure liege (the realm the title legally belongs to) of the character's primary title, without its tier word. The second is a fixed text. The key names (nomad_...) suggest it is for the nomad title decision, but the game's documentation does not say when each is used.

label: Door or tent flap
summary: One of two words: 'tent-flap' or 'door'.
details: Both are lower case. The game's documentation does not say what picks between them.

label: Door or tent flap (by key)
summary: The same words as GetDoor, 'tent-flap' or 'door', picked through the keys is_tentflap and is_door.
details: Each entry only repeats another text key ($tent_flap$, $door$) rather than holding its own words. In the game's text files those keys are most likely the same words as in GetDoor, but the input does not show them.

label: Dungeon or stockade
summary: One of two words: 'stockade' or 'Dungeon'.
details: Only the second is capitalised in the game's text. The game's documentation does not say what picks between them.

label: Dungeon link
summary: The words stockade or dungeon as a clickable game-concept link.
details: The texts are [stockade|E] and [dungeon|E]; the |E form makes the word a game-concept link.

label: Council proposal type
summary: Names the kind of change the current ecumenical council proposal makes to a tenet: make it core, permit it, prohibit it or let it be learned.
details: Runs on the council activity. The entries pull in the text keys for the four tenet statuses (core, permitted, prohibited, known).

label: Council doctrine proposal name
summary: The name of the first doctrine proposed in the council, or nothing when there is none.
details: The first entry reads the doctrine stored in the variable 'third_debate_proposal' of the saved scope ec_proposal_activity and gives its name as seen by the host's faith. The second entry is empty text.

label: Council doctrine result
summary: Text for how the first doctrine vote ended: ' passed' (highlighted) or ' status quo'.
details: Both texts start with a space, so they follow a word directly. 'Status quo' means nothing changed.

label: Council proposal log wording
summary: Wording for a set council proposal: a tenet status (core, permitted, prohibited, known) or a doctrine proposal (named or none).
details: Going by its name it is used for a log of the set proposal; the game's documentation does not say. Six entries exist; the input shows texts only for the first four, which are the four tenet status names. The two doctrine entries have the same keys as in GetEcumenicalCouncilDoctrine1Proposal.

label: Council first tenet proposal
summary: Names the kind of change the council's first tenet proposal makes: make it core, permit it, prohibit it or let it be learned.
details: The four texts are the tenet status names (core, permitted, prohibited, known). Same entries as GetEcumenicalCouncilCurrentProposal.

label: Council first tenet result
summary: Text for how the first tenet vote ended: ' passed' (highlighted) or ' status quo'.
details: Both texts begin with a space. 'Status quo' means nothing changed.

label: Council second tenet proposal
summary: Names the kind of change the council's second tenet proposal makes: make it core, permit it, prohibit it or let it be learned.
details: Same entries as the first-tenet version, but for the second tenet slot.

label: Council second tenet result
summary: Text for how the second tenet vote ended: ' passed' (highlighted) or ' status quo'.
details: Both texts begin with a space. 'Status quo' means nothing changed.

label: Debate tenet status link
summary: Going by its name, the status of the first debated tenet as a clickable link: core, permitted, prohibited, known or unknown.
details: Runs on a character. The game's documentation lists five entries; the input shows texts for the first four only (core, permitted, prohibited, known as game-concept links). The text of the fifth, 'unknown', is not shown.

label: Debate tenet status word
summary: Going by its name, the status of the first debated tenet as a plain word: Core, Permitted, Prohibited, Known or unknown.
details: The game's documentation lists five entries; the input shows texts for the first four only. The text of the fifth, 'unknown', is not shown.

label: Debate second tenet status link
summary: Going by its name, the status of the second debated tenet as a clickable link: core, permitted, prohibited, known or unknown.
details: Same entries as the first-tenet version. The text of the fifth entry, 'unknown', is not shown in the input.

label: Debate second tenet status word
summary: Going by its name, the status of the second debated tenet as a plain word: Core, Permitted, Prohibited, Known or unknown.
details: Same entries as the first-tenet version. The text of the fifth entry, 'unknown', is not shown in the input.

label: Education boost percent
summary: A percentage that depends on the education rank: 10%, 20%, 30% and 40% for ranks 1 to 4.
details: There are five ranks (education_rank_1 to 5). The input shows texts for the first four only, going up by ten points each; the text for rank 5 is not shown.

label: Education trait name
summary: The name of the character's education trait, such as 'Naive Appeaser' or 'Gray Eminence'.
details: There are 25 entries: five skills (diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue, learning) with five levels each. The input only shows texts for the first four diplomacy levels, so the other names are not listed here.

label: Education skill link
summary: The name of a skill as a clickable game-concept link: diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue or learning.
details: Five entries, one per skill (the keys end in _concept). The input shows texts for diplomacy, martial, stewardship and intrigue. Going by the name, it is meant for the skill of an education trait.

label: Er or im ending
summary: A short word ending: 'er' or 'im'.
details: The names of the entries say 'abbreviated'. The condition that picks one is not shown in the game's documentation.

label: Exam focus wording
summary: Going by its name, a phrase for the skill an exam is focused on: 'martial scholar', 'scholar of learning' or 'stewardship scholar'.
details: Runs on an activity. Only three skills are covered. The game's documentation does not say which activity it belongs to; the key names (exam_focus_...) point to an exam.

label: Exam score adjective
summary: An adjective for a character's exam score: perfect, heavenly, glorious, marvelous, respectable, proper, curious or quaint.
details: Eight entries, listed in this order in the game's documentation. The input shows texts for the first four. The game's documentation does not say which score gives which word.

label: Exotic pet
summary: The name of an exotic pet: Pet Wolf, Pet Bear, Pet Lion or Pet Tiger.
details: The names are capitalised like titles.

label: Expensive dessert (plural)
summary: The name of a costly dessert in plural form, such as 'saffron cakes' or 'candied figs'.
details: The game's documentation marks it Random Valid, so one of the entries may be picked at random. There are 21 entries; the input shows texts for four. Some entries link to a glossary word, like entremets.

label: Dessert in the face
summary: Going by its name, a single dessert with an article, such as 'a saffron cake' or 'a fig pie', for a dessert hitting someone in the face.
details: Marked Random Valid, so one entry may be picked at random. There are 14 entries (the keys end in _face); the input shows texts for four. The 'candied figs' key gives 'a fig pie', which is not literally the same dish.

label: Expensive drink (plural)
summary: The name of a costly drink in plural form, such as 'noble meads' or 'imported wines'.
details: Random Valid. The list has 32 entries covering wines, spirits, teas and other drinks. The input shows texts for the first four.

label: Expensive drink (singular)
summary: The name of a costly drink in singular form, such as 'Bordeaux claret' or 'imported wine'.
details: Random Valid. 29 entries (the plural list GetExpensiveDrink has 32). The first entry only reuses the text key of the plural hippocras. The input shows texts for four entries.

label: Expensive meal
summary: The name of a luxury dish, such as 'roast swan', 'veal cutlets' or 'fresh quail'.
details: Random Valid. 27 entries, including exotic dishes. The input shows texts for four.

label: Expensive meal (alternative)
summary: The name of a second set of luxury dishes: fine cheeses, almond eggs, sturgeon caviar, roast capon, eel pie or porpoise.
details: Random Valid. Works the same way as GetExpensiveMeal but with a different, smaller set of dishes.

label: Faith creation reaction
summary: A spoken line reacting to the creation of a new faith, one per kind of reaction: personal, heretical, frightened, crusader, interested or uninterested.
details: The entry keys are named after options of the event faith_creation.1001. Some of the lines name the high god of the character's faith (ROOT's faith); the frightened and crusader lines also name the other person's kind of unbeliever. The input shows texts for four.

label: Grand temple name
summary: The name of a grand temple building: Grand Basilica, Grand Mosque or Grand Temple.
details: The entries are holy-site building keys. The game's documentation does not say what picks one.

label: Faith sacred language
summary: The name of a language that is sacred to a faith, such as Latin, Aramaic or Arabic, with a fallback.
details: The game's documentation gives its scope as 'all', so it works in any scope. The list has 17 entries, with the Greek name appearing twice. The last, fallback_liturgical_province_language, is a fallback. The input shows texts for four.

label: Character's sacred language
summary: The name of a language that is sacred to a faith, such as Latin or Arabic, with a fallback, run on a character.
details: The same languages as GetFaithSacredLanguage but runs on a character and has a different fallback (fallback_liturgical_character_language).

label: Tax exempt institution
summary: Going by its name, the institution a faith's tax exemption applies to: 'the Church' or 'charities'.
details: Two plain text entries (keys faithtaxexemption_...). The game's documentation says nothing more.

label: Faith temple
summary: The word for a temple building: church, mosque, monastery or temple.
details: All four words are lower case. The entries are temple building keys.

label: House feud long story
summary: A sentence telling how a house feud began, such as a personal rivalry, a killing, an imprisonment or a broken wedding.
details: Runs on a house relation. The texts read variables like house_feud_victim and house_feud_attacker saved on the root and name the characters involved. 23 entries; the input shows texts for four. Compare GetFamilyFeudShort for the short reason word.

label: House feud reason
summary: A short word for the reason behind a house feud: contempt, killing, imprisonment and more.
details: The game's documentation lists house_feud_hatred twice (both texts read 'contempt') and the last entry is a fallback. The input shows texts for the first four; the other reasons (torturing, blinding, castration and so on) are named only by their keys.

label: House feud short phrase
summary: A short phrase about the feud, built around the reason word, such as 'my killing of ...' or 'X's contempt with me'.
details: The entry keys name the attacker, the victim and a neutral character as the point of view. It builds on GetFamilyFeudShort and the saved variables house_feud_victim and house_feud_attacker. The game's documentation lists house_feud_verb_char_attacker twice.

label: House feud victim phrase
summary: A short phrase about the feud naming the victim, such as 'the contempt with <name>' or 'the killing of <name>'.
details: Uses GetFamilyFeudShort and the saved victim variable. The game's documentation lists house_feud_verb_victim twice.

label: Family relation plural
summary: The plural word for a family relation, such as sisters, brothers, aunts or uncles.
details: 18 entries in the game's documentation: siblings, aunts and uncles, nieces and nephews, children, grandchildren (granddaughter and grandson listed twice), grandparents, great-grandparents and kinsfolk. The input shows texts for the first four.

label: Far-off region
summary: The name of a distant land: Cathay, Sudan beyond the Sahara, India or the steppes.
details: Random Valid, so one region can be picked at random. The keys belong to the artifact book topics 'travels'.

label: Feline or canine
summary: The word 'feline' or 'canine'.
details: What decides between them is not given in the game's documentation.

label: Fighter term
summary: A word for a fighter: man-at-arms, soldier or warrior.
details: Singular, lower case. The game's documentation does not list what picks one.

label: Fighter term (plural)
summary: The plural word for fighters: men-at-arms, soldiers or warriors.
details: The plural counterpart of GetFighterTerm.

label: Fighter term (possessive)
summary: The possessive form of the fighter word: man-at-arms', soldier's or warrior's.
details: The possessive counterpart of GetFighterTerm.

label: Follower trait monologue
summary: A line of speech that matches one personality trait, such as 'people are so sensitive these days' for callous.
details: 36 entries named after personality traits (callous, sadistic, zealous, ...), all keyed to the event ep3_camp_party.2000. The lazy trait is listed twice. The texts use #EMP to stress words. The input shows texts for four.

label: Follower or vassal
summary: The word 'follower' or 'vassal'.
details: The game's documentation does not list what picks one.

label: Food bird
summary: The name of a bird: duck, chicken or goose.
details: Random Valid, so one is picked at random. Going by its name, it is used in food texts.

label: Food detail
summary: An ingredient word: coriander, lemon or almond.
details: Random Valid. The first key is named cilantro, but its text reads 'coriander'.

label: Friend noun
summary: A casual word for a friend: chum, pal, mucker, habibi or habiba.
details: Five entries. The input shows texts for the first four; the text of habiba is not shown.

label: Frostbitten body part
summary: The name of a body part, for frostbite wording: nose, ear, arm, hand, finger, leg, foot or toe.
details: Eight plain lower-case words. The input shows texts for the first four.

label: Gamekeepers term
summary: A term for hunt helpers: flushers, Masters of the Chase or gamekeepers.
details: By the key names, the first is for adventurers, the second for nomads and the third for regular rulers.

label: Alliterating animal
summary: The name of an animal: warthog or monkey.
details: The key names say 'gender' and 'alliterating', so it probably pairs an animal with the character's gender, but the game's documentation does not say which gender gets which.

label: Rite tenet sentence
summary: A sentence describing what a rite focused on a tenet stands for, one per tenet, such as 'This rite rejects sacred images ...'.
details: Works in any scope and is Random Valid. 97 entries: one per tenet plus a fallback. The input shows texts for the first four.

label: Tenet sentence
summary: A sentence describing what a tenet stands for, starting with the tenet's name as shown for the player's rite.
details: Works in any scope and is Random Valid. Mirrors GetGenericRiteTenetSentence but names the tenet instead of saying 'this rite'. 97 entries including a fallback. Wording can differ slightly, for example in the armed pilgrimages entry.

label: Government authority name
summary: The name of an authority type, as a clickable link: imperial bureaucracy, tribal authority, crown authority and so on.
details: Eight entries, run on a character; going by the name, it is the authority of the character's government. The input shows texts for the first four. The last is a generic government authority.

label: Government icon
summary: A clickable icon link for a government form, such as holy order, mercenary, adventurer or nomadic.
details: 20 entries, run on a character; the input shows texts for four. The texts end in _i, such as [holy_order_i|E].

label: Government type icon
summary: A clickable icon link for a government type, such as holy order, mercenary, adventurer or nomadic.
details: Runs on a government type instead of a character. The same list as GetGovernmentIcon without its first entry, the monastic holy order.

label: Governor small talk
summary: A line of small talk addressed to a fellow governor, one of ten; the four shown are about the chariot races of Byzantium.
details: Ten entries (chariot_governor_chitchat_1 to 10). The input shows the first four, which praise the Hippodrome and the races; the rest are not shown.

label: Governor title link
summary: The word for a governor as a clickable link: strategos or governor.
details: Two entries, STRATEGOS_CONCEPT and GOVERNOR_CONCEPT. The game's documentation does not say what picks one.

label: Governors title link (plural)
summary: The plural word for governors as a clickable link: strategoi or governors.
details: The plural counterpart of GetGovernorConcept.

label: Grotesque creature
summary: A creature from legend with a short description: cynocephalus, blemee or sciapod.
details: Random Valid. The texts end in a comma, so they are followed by more of the sentence.

label: Grotesque creatures (plural)
summary: The plural of the legendary creatures with a short description: cynocephaly, blemmyae or sciapodes.
details: Random Valid. The texts end in a comma. The blemmyae text starts with the singular 'blemmya'.

label: Guests or courtiers label
summary: A label for the court window: 'Your courtiers' or 'Your guests and courtiers'.
details: Runs on a character. The texts read the owner of the court window and use another custom text for the word 'courtiers'.

label: Guild type
summary: The name of a guild building in a province: guild halls, carvers guild, carpenters guild and so on.
details: Runs on a province and is Random Valid. Ten entries, the last a fallback. The input shows texts for four.

label: Heathen or miscreant
summary: The word 'heathen' or 'miscreant'.
details: The key names end in _concept, but the texts are plain words, not links. What decides between them is not shown.

label: Opposite pronoun 'him/her'
summary: The pronoun 'him' or 'her'.
details: Random Valid. The name says 'opposite', which suggests the other gender than the character's, but the game's documentation does not state it. The entry keys are the usual him/her pronoun keys.

label: Opposite pronoun 'his/her'
summary: The pronoun 'his' or 'her'.
details: Random Valid. Same idea as GetHerHimOpposite, but the possessive form. The 'opposite' meaning is only a guess from the name.

label: Heroine or hero
summary: The word 'heroine' or 'hero'.
details: Two entries. The game's documentation does not list what decides between them.

label: Heroine's or hero's
summary: The possessive 'heroine's' or 'hero's'.
details: The possessive counterpart of GetHeroineHero.

label: HoF greeting exchange
summary: A phrase for how two people greet one another, in third person, such as 'they share an overlong embrace' or 'they have a joyous and laughter-filled exchange'.
details: Nine entries, from tender embraces (brotherly and sisterly) through joyous, courteous, brief and tense to loud and openly hostile. The input shows texts for four. The game's documentation does not say what 'HoF' stands for or where it is used.

label: HoF greeting (first person)
summary: A phrase for how two people greet each other, from the speaker's side, such as 'we share a joyous embrace' or 'we have a brief and courteous exchange'.
details: Seven entries, from subtle and joyous embraces to curt, angry and insulting ones. The input shows texts for four. The game's documentation does not say what 'HoF' stands for.

label: Holy compliment
summary: A flattering word: almighty, most omnipotent, divine, venerable or reverent.
details: Random Valid, so one is picked at random. The input shows texts for four.

label: Homage speech (liege's view)
summary: A paragraph from the liege's side describing how a vassal's homage speech went: stutter, lisp, wheeze or slow.
details: The texts use pronouns and the name of the root character, who is the one giving homage, and describe a speech impediment or nervousness.

label: Homage speech (vassal's view)
summary: A first-person paragraph describing how the vassal's own homage speech went: stutter, lisp, wheeze or slow.
details: The counterpart of GetHomageDeliveryDescLiege, written from the vassal's point of view.

label: Hunt description
summary: The long description text of the hunt, one for adventurers and one for regular rulers.
details: Both begin with the same intro about thrills and danger. The adventurer version adds that hunting gives less prestige but provides provisions, that the hunt is overseen by the huntperson camp officer, and that at the start the player can buy hunting rights for gold, else they gain experience on the poacher track of the Gallowsbait trait. The regular version names the master of the hunt, who announces sightings of beasts common, rare and fierce.

label: Hunt attendee label
summary: A label for a hunt attendee: 'Female Attendee', 'Male Attendee' or just 'Attendee'.
details: The three entries are named female, male and equal. The game's documentation does not say what picks one; the 'equal' entry gives the plain 'Attendee'.

label: Huntmaster title
summary: The title of the person who oversees the hunt: the camp officer's position name for adventurers, 'Master of the Hunt' otherwise.
details: The adventurer entry reads the name of the court position huntperson_camp_officer without a tooltip; the regular entry is fixed text.

label: Huntmaster title (tooltip)
summary: The name of the court position that oversees the hunt, with its tooltip: the huntperson camp officer for adventurers, the master of the hunt otherwise.
details: Like GetHuntMasterDesc, but both entries read the position name from the game, using the form with a tooltip.

label: Imperial family type
summary: The name of a family group as a label: 'Regent Family' or 'Imperial Family'.
details: Two entries named after game concepts.

label: Inside or outside realm note
summary: A short coloured note beside a character: inside your realm, not inside your realm, independent, or the title of their top liege.
details: Oddly, the key not_in_realm_current_situation gives '(inside your realm)' and in_realm_current_situation gives '(not inside your realm)', which looks swapped. The landless entries show 'Independent' or the primary title of the second character's top liege.

label: Alliance info by realm
summary: A hint about allying with a character: a vassal ally can't join factions, but you can't call them to war; a character outside the realm has soldiers that could help in your wars.
details: The second text reads the military strength of the other character (the second scope) and shows it with a soldier icon.

label: Background detail
summary: A small scene detail for flavor, such as 'a servant struggling with a vase' or 'a fly crawling on some gilded decorations'.
details: Random Valid, so one is picked at random. Eleven entries; the input shows texts for four.

label: Title holder or title name
summary: The title holder's short name if someone holds it, otherwise 'the' plus the title's own name.
details: Runs on a title. The first entry shows the holder, the second 'the' plus the title's base name for an uncreated title.

label: Title holder pronoun
summary: A pronoun: 'her', 'his' or 'its'.
details: Runs on a title. The entry keys are the usual her/his/its pronoun keys; by the name it is for the title's holder, with 'its' presumably for a title without one, but the game's documentation does not say.

label: Injured body part
summary: The name of an injured body part: missing leg, eye, eyes, testicles or face.
details: The key 'testacles' is a typo in the game's own data, but its text reads 'testicles'. The input shows texts for the first four; the text of the face entry is not shown.

label: Inspiration material
summary: A material word for an inspiration: leafs, metal, jewel, fabric and so on.
details: Random Valid. Eleven entries including writing, sweat, wood, stone, clay and ingredients; the wood key is listed twice. The last is a fallback.

label: Inspiration owner type
summary: The kind of creator an inspiration belongs to: writer, weaponsmith, armorer, weaver and so on.
details: Eleven entries including adventurer, artisan, alchemist, researcher and theologian, with a fallback.

label: Inspiration topic
summary: The subject of an inspiration: pleasantry, battle, organization, cunning and so on.
details: Seven entries for diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue, learning, travel and pilgrimage. The input shows texts for the first four skills.

label: Inspiration object
summary: The thing being made for an inspiration: book, weapon, armor, tapestry, banner and so on.
details: The weapon and armor entries read the base type from another custom text. A fallback entry is included.

label: Inspiration room
summary: The room for the creative work: study, smithy, armory, weavery and so on.
details: Nine entries, the last a fallback.

label: Inspiration work station
summary: The work spot for the creative work: desk, bellows, anvil, forge and so on.
details: Eleven entries, including loom, maps, bench, cauldron, alembic and library, with a fallback.

label: Inspiration tool
summary: The tool for the creative work: quill, tongs, hammer, shuttle and so on.
details: Random Valid. Twelve entries, with a fallback.

label: Inspiration verb
summary: The verb for the creative work, such as write, forge, weave or go, in the present/future wording.
details: Each entry calls another custom text on the character, like InspirationWritePresentFuture. The make entry appears twice in the game's documentation.

label: Intrigue building
summary: The name of a building: Markets, Keep, Tradeport or Bustling Metropolis.
details: Random Valid, so one is picked at random. The key name links it to intrigue, but the game's documentation says nothing about why these four buildings.

label: Invalidated contract text
summary: Text saying a task contract became invalid, naming its type, such as 'Transport VIP contract'.
details: 24 entries (keys invalidated_laamp_...), covering transport, raid, join war, help claimant, construction and more. The text reads the name of the task contract type and adds 'contract'. The last entry is invalidated_laamp_base_4100.

label: Activity invitation flavor
summary: The flavor sentence in an invitation to an activity, depending on the activity: tournament, wedding, feast, hunt, pilgrimage, funeral, coronation, examination and more.
details: 28 entries, with the examination entry listed twice. Texts may name the current phase or location of the activity the character is in. A fallback is included. The input shows texts for the first four.
